items.title: Pure-core burn-alert evaluator over usage-sweep session rows
items.context: New packages/main/src/core/usage-burn-alert.ts: evaluate SweepSessionRow[] against injected thresholds (nowMs and thresholds passed in; no process.env or Date.now inside, matching the usage-sweep pure-core contract). Flags a session when transcript file size exceeds the byte threshold, cumulative input tokens exceed the token threshold (codex: last cumulative total_token_usage input; claude: summed input + cacheRead + cacheCreation), or the session is older than the age threshold while still recently active. Read-only: stat only, never writes.

happy.desc: evaluateBurnAlerts flags a codex session whose file size exceeds the byte threshold (strictly greater), returning a finding with reason=file-size naming the session file and exceeded threshold
evaluateBurnAlerts flags a codex session whose last cumulative total_token_usage inputTokens exceeds the token threshold (strictly greater), returning reason=input-tokens
evaluateBurnAlerts flags a claude session whose summed (inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens) exceeds the token threshold, returning reason=input-tokens
evaluateBurnAlerts flags a session whose firstTimestamp is older than ageDays while the session mtime falls inside the recent-activity scan window, returning reason=session-age
evaluateBurnAlerts returns an empty array for rows that are all below every threshold
A single session can trip multiple reasons simultaneously (e.g. file-size AND input-tokens); all triggered reasons appear in the finding
Findings are returned in a deterministic order (stable sort by session file or sessionId) regardless of input row order

edge.desc: A session with usage exactly AT the threshold (not strictly greater) is NOT flagged; only strictly-greater trips the alert
A session with null usage (unknown) is never flagged for input-tokens, even when other thresholds are set
A session with null or unparseable firstTimestamp is never flagged for session-age
A codex session with inputTokens=0 and a claude session with all-zero usage fields are not flagged for input-tokens
fileSizeOf injection: when fileSizeOf is not provided the evaluator stats the file; when fileSizeOf IS provided it uses the injected function (test seam for OS-temp fixtures)
An empty rows array returns an empty findings array without error
A session whose firstTimestamp is within ageDays (recent session, not old) is never flagged for session-age even if the file is very large

adversarial.desc: The module does NOT import Date.now or process.env anywhere; nowMs and thresholds are injected arguments -- verified by source grep showing zero Date.now/process.env references in the file
The module does NOT import from core/usage-ledger (independence contract inherited from usage-sweep); verified by source grep
evaluateBurnAlerts never writes to the filesystem: calling it with real session paths leaves those files byte-identical (zero-writes assertion on mtime+size snapshot before/after)
A session row whose file path does not exist on disk (stale/deleted transcript) does not throw; the file-size check gracefully skips or reports 0
Rows with NaN, Infinity, or negative token counts do not cause the evaluator to throw or produce corrupt findings

items.title: Env-tunable threshold resolver with conservative defaults
items.context: Resolver maps an env record to thresholds: LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_FILE_MB (default 100), LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS (default 100000000), LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_AGE_DAYS (default 7), LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS (default 48, scan window; 0 disables the doctor burn scan). Pure function of the env record so it is testable; handlers pass process.env.

happy.desc: resolveBurnAlertThresholds({}) returns the four defaults: fileSizeBytes=104857600 (100MB), inputTokens=100000000, ageDays=7, recentHours=48
resolveBurnAlertThresholds with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_FILE_MB=50 returns fileSizeBytes=52428800 (50*1024*1024) while other defaults are unchanged
resolveBurnAlertThresholds with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=500000 returns inputTokens=500000 while other defaults are unchanged
resolveBurnAlertThresholds with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_AGE_DAYS=14 returns ageDays=14 while other defaults are unchanged
resolveBurnAlertThresholds with LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 returns recentHours=0 (disables the doctor scan); verified the doctor scan is skipped downstream when recentHours=0
resolveBurnAlertThresholds with all four env vars set returns all four overridden values

edge.desc: Garbage string env value (e.g. LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_FILE_MB=abc) falls back to the default for that field without throwing
Negative env value (e.g. LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_AGE_DAYS=-5) falls back to the default for that field without throwing
Zero value for FILE_MB/INPUT_TOKENS/AGE_DAYS falls back to default (zero is not a meaningful threshold); RECENT_HOURS=0 is the intentional disable sentinel and is kept
Floating-point env value (e.g. LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_FILE_MB=1.5) is handled: either truncated to integer or falls back to default, but never throws
Empty string env value falls back to default without throwing
Very large env value (e.g. LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=999999999999999) is accepted without overflow or NaN

adversarial.desc: resolveBurnAlertThresholds is a pure function of the env record argument; it does NOT read process.env directly -- verified by source grep showing zero process.env references in core/usage-burn-alert.ts
Env record with prototype-pollution keys (__proto__, constructor) does not pollute the return value or throw
Calling resolveBurnAlertThresholds with an env record containing only unrelated keys (e.g. HOME, PATH) returns all four defaults unchanged

items.title: usage_sweep --alert exit-nonzero mode
items.context: usage_sweep gains an --alert boolean: the report is computed and printed as today, alert evaluation runs over the swept rows, flagged sessions are listed, and the CLI exits non-zero when any alert fired (recover_evidence dispatch pattern: print result first, then throw) so a cron job can drive notifications. --alert performs zero writes and stays effectively readOnly for ownership/activity/hook classification.

happy.desc: usage_sweep --alert with sessions exceeding thresholds prints the structured alert report (flagged sessions with reasons) to stdout, then exits non-zero (exitCode=1)
usage_sweep --alert with no sessions exceeding any threshold prints the report and exits zero (no alerts fired)

usage_sweep --alert prints the normal sweep report FIRST (human or JSON mode), then appends the alert evaluation section, matching the recover_evidence dispatch pattern (print result first, then throw so exitCode=1)
usage_sweep --alert --json returns a JSON object including both the sweep report fields and an alerts array with the flagged findings
Plain usage_sweep (without --alert) behavior is unchanged: no alert evaluation, exit code 0 regardless of session token counts

edge.desc: usage_sweep --alert with --since covering zero sessions (empty stores or all files older than cutoff) prints clean report and exits zero
usage_sweep --alert with custom threshold env vars (e.g. LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_INPUT_TOKENS=1) fires on sessions that would not trip defaults
usage_sweep --alert combined with --out still writes the report file (exclusive-create fence) AND prints+throws on alert; the --out write happens before the alert throw
usage_sweep --alert with --json outputs valid JSON even when alerts fire (the throw happens after the structured result is printed, not mid-JSON)

adversarial.desc: usage_sweep --alert performs zero writes to the codex/claude store directories: before/after mtime+size snapshot of fixture stores is identical

usage_sweep --alert does NOT modify ownership-gate.ts or activity-policy.ts classification; the command stays effectively readOnly for ownership/activity/hook classification -- verified by confirming isReadOnlyCommand returns true for usage_sweep
usage_sweep --alert does NOT change the shouldWriteActivityLog result for the usage_sweep command (inherits existing activity-policy classification)
usage_sweep (plain, no --alert) does NOT evaluate alerts or exit non-zero even when sessions have astronomical token counts; the --alert flag is the sole trigger
The --alert flag is registered in the command catalog schema so the CLI parser accepts it; an unregistered flag would cause a parse error before the handler runs
